summary: Robert Mayer is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Bristol (dissertation, to 1985) and completed his Ph.D. at Leiden University under Tilmann Vetter, Alexis Sanderson, and Pieter Cornelis Verhagen. He joined the University of Oxford faculty in 2002.

Robert Needham Cust was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Eton College, Trinity College, Cambridge, East India Company College, Haileybury, and Fort William College. He served in the Bengal Civil Service from circa 1843 to 1867.

Robert P. Goldman is an Indologist who earned his A.B. at Columbia and Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher, also studying under Shivram Dattatray Joshi, T. S. Srinivasa Sastri, and Shrinivasa Shastri. He became a professor at UC Berkeley around 1971.

Robert S. Ellwood was a religious studies and Japanology scholar who studied at the University of Colorado, Yale University, and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade. He held an academic post at the University of Southern California from circa 1967 to 1997.

Robert S. Nelson is an art historian who studied at Rice University and New York University. He served as a professor at the University of Chicago (~1978–2005) before joining Yale University circa 2005.

Robert S. P. Beekes was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Leiden University (~1956–1969) under doctoral supervisor F. B. J. Kuiper. He held posts at Marnix Gymnasium and Leiden University (1973, 1979).
Robert Sewell was an Indologist and historian who served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1868 to 1896 and held the post of Keeper at the Tamil Nadu Archives.
Robert Seymour Conway was a linguist who was educated at the City of London School (~1879–1883). He held posts at Newnham College (~1887–1893) and Gonville and Caius College (~1888–1894).
Robert Warren Clark is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under doctoral supervisor Karen Christina Lang and adviser K. L. Seshagiri Rao.

Robert Zimmermann was an Indologist who studied at St Beuno's Jesuit Spirituality Centre and the University of Berlin. He served as Professor of Sanskrit and ancient Indian philosophy at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1914–1930) and led the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

Robin Coningham is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who earned his PhD from the University of Cambridge under Raymond Allchin. He was a professor at the University of Bradford (1994–2005) and became Professor of Early Medieval Archaeology at Durham University in 2005.
Robin D. S. Yates is a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology who earned his PhD from Harvard University (~1974–1980). Around 1993, he took up a James McGill Professorship at McGill University.

Robin Dunbar studied at Magdalen College School and Magdalen College before completing his doctoral studies under John Crook (~1969–1974). He held a post at University College London from circa 1987 to 1994.

Roderick M. Chisholm was a philosopher who studied at Brown and Harvard (Ph.D.). He held professorships at the Barnes Foundation (1946) and Brown University (~1947–1987), served as president of the Metaphysical Society of America (1973), and edited Philosophy and Phenomenological Research.
Roderick S. Bucknell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who held posts at the University of Queensland, serving as Associate Professor from circa 1990 to 2002.

Roderick Whitfield is a scholar of history, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the British Museum (attested 1986), the University of London, and SOAS University of London, where he was attested as professor emeritus in 2011.

Roger Bischoff is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Mother Sayamagyi and U Chit Tin, and served as an Assistant Teacher at the International Meditation Centre (attested 1995).
Roger Brown was a scholar of linguistics who completed his studies at the University of Michigan (~1945–1952). He subsequently served on the faculty at Harvard University from 1962 to 1994.
Roger Heim was a scientist who studied at École Centrale Paris and the Science Faculty of Paris. He held a post at the Muséum national d'histoire naturelle from circa 1929 to 1972.

Roger R. Jackson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned his degrees at Wesleyan and Wisconsin–Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa. He taught at Fairfield University (attested 1986) and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Carleton College (attested 1990–2006).
